overview: Two major plant growth hormones with overlapping growth-promoting effects but very different signature roles.
genZNote: Auxin: the hormone behind bending toward light. Gibberellin: the hormone behind sudden growth spurts.

aspects.label: Signature Effect
aspects.valueA: Promotes cell elongation and is central to phototropism and apical dominance.
aspects.valueB: Promotes stem elongation (bolting) and breaks seed/bud dormancy.

aspects.label: Classic Site of Action
aspects.valueA: Concentrated at the shoot tip, controlling directional growth.
aspects.valueB: Especially active in stems, causing dramatic internode elongation.

aspects.label: Role in Apical Dominance
aspects.valueA: Directly responsible for suppressing lateral bud growth (apical dominance).
aspects.valueB: Does not primarily control apical dominance.

aspects.label: Classic Demonstration
aspects.valueA: Discovered via Charles and Francis Darwin's coleoptile phototropism experiments.
aspects.valueB: Discovered from studies on 'foolish seedling disease' in rice caused by the fungus Gibberella fujikuroi.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Gibberellin's discovery from a fungal disease of rice (bakanae) is a frequently asked history-of-science fact.
overlay.memoryTrick: Auxin = bending toward light. Gibberellin = growing tall fast (bolting).
overlay.commonMisconception: Auxin isn't only about phototropism — it also plays a major role in root initiation and fruit development.
